subject: Dedicated commit: tiering proposal + memory/perf tradeoffs
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@datafolio.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit: tiering proposal + memory/perf tradeoffs

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I put together two committed-capacity options that map to the DataFolio workload profile you shared (heavy 65B/70B generation at 1–2k concurrent sessions; steady inference windows). The attached spreadsheet (redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.xlsx) has the math; key points below so you can share with the procurement team quickly: 

Option A — H100-first (higher perf/$ for long sequences)
- 24x H100 80GB
- Target sustained throughput: 1.8k concurrent gen sessions (95th pct latency SLOs)
- Monthly committed tokens: 3.2B
- Baseline discount: 25% off hosted list

Option B — Mixed tier (cost-optimized)
- 18x H100 80GB + 12x L40S 48GB
- Routing policy: latency-critical traffic prefer H100, batch-heavy shorter sessions to L40S
- Monthly committed tokens: 3.2B (same)
- Baseline discount: 21% off hosted list

Tradeoffs to flag for engineering:
- Memory: L40S has less effective per-instance model residency for very large KV caches; if you maintain long-context caching the H100 mix reduces remote fetches.
- Perf/$: for long sequences and 70B models H100 shows ~1.6x perf improvement; L40S gives ~1.2x but at ~40% lower hourly cost.
- Throughput SLOs: we can guarantee 95th pct latency SLOs for Option A under the committed token shape; Option B uses smart routing and cache pinning to meet a 95th pct for 80% of traffic and 99th pct for critical routes routed to H100.

Concessions we can discuss: a modest additional discount for multi-year or accelerated payment, and a two-week canary of the hybrid fleet before the full cutover (we run the canary on your prod traffic shadowed to us, no change to your infra).

I attached the detailed pricing and an initial canary playbook. If you want, I can loop in Vivek (sales leader) to approve deeper concessions, and have Stephanie scope a short perf-run plan with your infra team. What would you like us to prioritize — lower unit cost or tighter latency SLAs?

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), canary_playbook.md (doc)

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@datafolio.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@datafolio.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit: tiering proposal + memory/perf tradeoffs

Monica —

Thanks for the clear options and the sheet. Quick follow-ups from procurement + infra: 

1) Can we swap ~25% of the H100 capacity in Option A to L40S to reduce cost and still meet our target throughput? Our peak traffic has a lot of short sessions and we think batching can push more to cheaper cards.
2) For the hybrid (Option B) can you share an explicit perf/$ comparison for our 65B model (we use a 32k context with dense KV caching)? Specifically: expected tokens/sec per GPU and expected memory residency (KV cache hit rates assumptions).
3) Pricing: procurement is looking for something in the 28–30% effective discount range given our 12–18 month commit. Any room to bridge to that?

If it helps, I can set a 30‑minute call with our infra lead next week to walk through the KV/cache behavior. Also need standard procurement items — updated quote, SOW, and DocuSign once terms are locked.

Emma
Emma Liu
Director of ML Platforms, DataFolio
emma.liu@datafolio.ai

Subject: Re: Dedicated commit: tiering proposal + memory/perf tradeoffs

Emma —

Appreciate the concrete asks. I looped in Stephanie to give exact perf numbers and Vivek to weigh in on commercial flexibility. High-level answers below while Stephanie pulls numbers for your 65B profile: 

1) Swapping 25% H100 -> L40S is doable operationally. The effect on tail latency depends on your traffic mix — for steady long-context sessions we recommend pinning those workloads to H100 nodes and letting short interactive sessions go to L40S.

2) Perf/$ for 65B (early estimates from our lab):
- H100 80GB: ~115 tokens/sec (single-stream) at baseline perf; excellent KV cache residency for 32k.
- L40S 48GB: ~70 tokens/sec (single-stream) but batch throughput scales well for short sessions; memory-limited cache residency will reduce hit-rate for very long contexts unless you shard KV or use prefix-caching.
- Net: blended perf (if 25% swap) drops ~12–18% for long single-stream loads but improves cost by ~22–28% on infra spend.

3) Pricing: Vivek — do you have headroom for the 28–30% range with a 12–18 month commit? If not, Monica can propose a staged concession (start at 25% with an upgrade path if they hit committed tokens).

I attached a revised quote (redwood_revised_quote_20270630.pdf) that models the 25% swap and two commercial levers: 12‑month prepay vs 18‑month commit with quarterly true-ups. We also included a short canary plan (canary_playbook.md) — 2 weeks shadowing, automated rollback triggers, and a 1% waiver of overage fees during the trial window.

Let me know when you want to review live; happy to do a technical walkthrough with your infra lead.

—Monica

Attachments: redwood_revised_quote_20270630.pdf (quote)

Quick internal note on concessions:
- We can approve a 5% additional discount on top of the Option A baseline (so A becomes ~30%) for a 12‑month prepay.

- For the 25% H100->L40S swap, make sure the SOW calls out the routing policy and the cache pinning rules — otherwise we risk an SLA miss. Stephanie, can you confirm the rollout checklist so I can sign off commercially?

Vivek

1) Please add explicit wording to the SOW that DataFolio can request a one-time re-tier (25% swap) within the first 90 days post-cutover if observed traffic materially differs (with a defined measurement window and rollback terms).
2) Send the DocuSign link + updated quote (reflecting the 12‑month prepay at the 30% effective discount) so we can circulate to finance.

Appreciate the quick cadence.

Emma
